key_insight: TGSR-PINN improves PINN inverse transfer learning by using target-evidence to selectively soften source representations, reducing negative transfer while better recovering physical parameters.
engineering_relevance: This offers a practical transfer-learning strategy for physics-based inverse problems where accurate parameter identification matters as much as low field error.
method: Transfer only source network weights and biases; initialize target physical parameters separately.
After brief target adaptation, score neurons using first-order Taylor sensitivity and pre-activation variance on fixed batches.
Convert low-score evidence into weak-adaptation signals with a GMM and apply selective soft decay to affected input weight rows and biases.
evidence_signal: The method is reported to improve target parameter recovery while keeping field accuracy comparable on high-Péclet 2D advection-diffusion, Allen–Cahn to Burgers transfer, and a 5% noise reaction–diffusion case.
watch_item: The scoring and GMM-based reweighting depend on stable target batches and hyperparameter choices, so robustness across broader PDE families and noise regimes remains a concern.
paper_title: Target-Guided Selective Reweighting for Physics-Informed Neural Network Inverse Problems: A Transfer Learning Approach
